records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:138 compares hostnames case-sensitively despite DNS hostnames being case-insensitive, causing https://EXAMPLE.com/user to display only EXAMPLE.com for instance example.com. Normalize hostname case before comparison.
records.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the code at line 138 uses direct string comparison (==) between website_host and discourse_host without normalizing case. DNS hostnames are case-insensitive per RFC, but Ruby string comparison is case-sensitive. The diff shows: `if website_host == discourse_host` and `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')`. If a user enters 'https://EXAMPLE.com/user' and the instance is 'example.com', the comparison would fail, returning just 'EXAMPLE.com' instead of 'EXAMPLE.com/user'. This is a real correctness bug.
